rubrics_metrics.name: Use of original texts and documentary evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: "Whenever a point could be established by the aid of written documents, I have had recourse to the original text, and to the most authentic and approved works. I have cited my authorities in the notes, and anyone may refer to them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorial standard: prefer original documents for documentary claims and provide citations/notes to allow verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroborate important or doubtful testimony with multiple witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: "Whenever an opinion, a political custom, or a remark on the manners of the country was concerned, I endeavoured to consult the most enlightened men I met with. If the point in question was important or doubtful, I was not satisfied with one testimony, but I formed my opinion on the evidence of several witnesses."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard: do not rely on a single testimony for important or doubtful claims; seek multiple independent sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect confidential sources and withhold names when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The author carefully abstained from quoting names he heard in private conversations in order to avoid injuring the success of his statements or repaying hospitality by subsequent chagrin and annoyance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard: withhold identifying details when disclosure would breach confidences or cause harm; preserve source privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid shaping facts to fit ideas; base theory on mass of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The author asserts he has "never, knowingly, moulded facts to ideas, instead of ideas to facts" and that his judgment is formed "not on any single reason, but upon the mass of evidence."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research/interpretive principle: derive ideas from aggregated evidence rather than selecting facts to support a preconceived theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and declaring aims beyond party interests
rubrics_metrics.description: The book is written to favor no particular views; the author has "entertained no designs of serving or attacking any party; I have undertaken not to see differently, but to look further than parties."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly/political writing standard: aim for neutrality and long-term perspective rather than partisan advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetorical method: push ideas to theoretical extremes in discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: The author notes that "the author who wishes to be understood is obliged to push all his ideas to their utmost theoretical consequences, and often to the verge of what is false or impracticable;" he distinguishes normative discourse from action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges a stylistic/scientific device: in theoretical exposition, pursue consequences fully even if impractical in practice, but clarify the distinction.
